title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) & WebSockets Extensions for Real-Time DOM Morphing

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Normally, your browser has to ask the server for updates. With the SSE or WebSocket extension, the server keeps an open phone line to your page. Whenever a new chat message or live price arrives, the server speaks an HTML fragment through the line, and HTMX immediately slots it onto your screen in real time.
progressiveExplaining.junior: HTMX supports real-time updates via official extensions: `sse.js` and `ws.js`. For Server-Sent Events: `<div hx-ext="sse" sse-connect="/events" sse-swap="message">`. The element connects to the SSE stream and swaps incoming HTML payloads directly into the DOM. For WebSockets: `<div hx-ext="ws" ws-connect="/chat">` allows both receiving HTML pushes and sending form payloads over the WebSocket connection (`ws-send`).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, HTMX real-time extensions stream pure HTML over persistent bi-directional WebSockets or un-directional SSE connections. This unifies real-time streaming with hypermedia: rather than parsing JSON payloads in JavaScript and running client-side template engines to update views, the server streams live HTML fragments (e.g. `<tr>...</tr>` or OOB swaps) that HTMX immediately mounts into the DOM.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: The `sse` extension instantiates a native `EventSource`. When `eventSource.onmessage` or a named event fires, the extension parses the message string, extracts OOB elements, and invokes the HTMX swap engine (`htmx.swap()`). The `ws` extension creates a `WebSocket` instance; on message receipt, it swaps the HTML, and on form submission inside `ws-send`, it serializes form values into JSON or query format and sends them over `socket.send()`.

interviewGotchas.question: What format must the server send when pushing messages over Server-Sent Events (SSE) to HTMX?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of the SSE wire protocol and HTMX integration.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer:
The server must format responses according to the W3C SSE standard with an event name and HTML data string. For example: ```http event: new_message data:
Hello World!
``` The `event:` name matches `sse-swap="new_message"`, and the `data:` contains the raw HTML fragment to swap.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: SSE messages require two trailing newline characters (`\n\n`) to flush the event over the HTTP stream.

interviewGotchas.question: Can you use Out-of-Band (`hx-swap-oob`) updates over WebSockets and SSE in HTMX?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of multi-target updates in real-time streams.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. A single SSE or WebSocket push event can contain both the main HTML fragment and multiple elements with `hx-swap-oob="true" id="..."`. HTMX will update the main target and simultaneously update all matching OOB elements across the entire page.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Ensure OOB elements sent over WebSockets have unique IDs that match existing DOM elements on the client.
